questions.q: What is the correct order of the first three stages of the Lockheed Martin Cyber Kill Chain?
options: Reconnaissance, Weaponization, Delivery
Delivery, Reconnaissance, Weaponization
Weaponization, Delivery, Reconnaissance
Installation, Reconnaissance, Delivery
questions.explain: The kill chain begins with Reconnaissance (researching the target), then Weaponization (building the attack tool), then Delivery (getting it to the target).

questions.q: In the Cyber Kill Chain, what happens during the 'Command & Control' stage?
options: The attacker researches the target's employees
The compromised system communicates back to an attacker-controlled server, giving the attacker a remote channel
The attacker builds the malicious payload
The final objective, like data theft, is achieved
questions.explain: Command & Control (C2) is the channel the compromised system uses to phone home, letting the attacker issue remote commands.

questions.q: What is the MITRE ATT&CK framework?
options: A seven-stage linear model identical to the kill chain
A free, publicly maintained knowledge base of real-world adversary tactics and techniques, each with its own documented ID
A proprietary tool only available to U.S. government agencies
A list of approved antivirus vendors
questions.explain: MITRE ATT&CK is a public, continuously updated matrix of documented real-world tactics and techniques used by defenders and vendors industry-wide.

questions.q: What is the difference between a 'tactic' and a 'technique' in the ATT&CK framework?
options: There is no difference — they're the same thing
A tactic is the attacker's goal at a given stage; a technique is the specific method used to achieve that goal
A technique is always more general than a tactic
Tactics only apply to nation-state actors
questions.explain: A tactic describes the 'why' (e.g. Persistence), while a technique describes the specific 'how' (e.g. a particular registry-key method).

questions.q: Why do SOC analysts typically reference both the kill chain and MITRE ATT&CK when triaging an incident?
options: The kill chain gives the narrative of where the attack is in its life cycle, while ATT&CK gives the technical precision of exactly which technique was used
Because only one of the two frameworks is ever accurate
Because regulations require citing both regardless of usefulness
Because ATT&CK replaced the kill chain and both are kept only for historical reasons
questions.explain: The kill chain explains the overall stage and urgency of an attack, while ATT&CK pinpoints the specific documented technique, which is useful for building detections.
